cases.sentence: Подъезжая домой в самом веселом расположении духа, Левин услыхал колокольчик со стороны ___ к дому.
cases.explain: «главного подъезда» — after the preposition «со», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: As he rode up to the house in the happiest frame of mind, Levin heard the bell ring at the side of the principal entrance of the house.

cases.sentence: «Да, это с ___, – подумал он, – самое время московского поезда…
cases.explain: «железной дороги» — after the preposition «с», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Yes, that’s someone from the railway station,” he thought, “just the time to be here from the Moscow train … Who could it be? What if it’s brother Nikolay? He did say: ‘Maybe I’ll go to the waters, or maybe I’ll come down to you.’ ” He felt dismayed and vexed for the first minute, that his brother Nikolay’s presence should come to disturb his happy mood of spring. But he felt ashamed of the feeling, and at once he opened, as it were, the arms of his soul, and with a softened feeling of joy and expectation, now he hoped with all his heart that it was his brother. He pricked up his horse, and riding out from behind the acacias he saw a hired three-horse sledge from the railway station, and a gentleman in a fur coat. It was not his brother. “Oh, if it were only some nice person one could talk to a little!” he thought.

cases.explain: «весеннее расположение» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: – А! – радостно прокричал Левин, поднимая обе руки кверху. – Вот ___!
cases.explain: «радостный-то гость» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Ah,” cried Levin joyfully, flinging up both his hands. “Here’s a delightful visitor! Ah, how glad I am to see you!” he shouted, recognizing Stepan Arkadyevitch.

cases.sentence: Желательнее было бы хорошенькую горничную в фартучке; но с твоим монашеством и ___ – это очень хорошо.
cases.explain: «строгим стилем» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Well, I am glad I managed to get away to you! Now I shall understand what the mysterious business is that you are always absorbed in here. No, really, I envy you. What a house, how nice it all is! So bright, so cheerful!” said Stepan Arkadyevitch, forgetting that it was not always spring and fine weather like that day. “And your nurse is simply charming! A pretty maid in an apron might be even more agreeable, perhaps; but for your severe monastic style it does very well.”

cases.sentence: Степан Аркадьич рассказал много ___ и в особенности интересную для Левина новость, что брат его Сергей Иванович собирался на нынешнее лето к нему в деревню.
cases.explain: «интересных новостей» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Stepan Arkadyevitch told him many interesting pieces of news; especially interesting to Levin was the news that his brother, Sergey Ivanovitch, was intending to pay him a visit in the summer.

cases.sentence: – Отлично, отлично, – говорил он, закуривая толстую папиросу после жаркого. – Я к тебе точно с парохода после шума и тряски на ___ вышел.
cases.explain: «тихий берег» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Splendid, splendid!” he said, lighting a fat cigar after the roast. “I feel as if, coming to you, I had landed on a peaceful shore after the noise and jolting of a steamer. And so you maintain that the laborer himself is an element to be studied and to regulate the choice of methods in agriculture. Of course, I’m an ignorant outsider; but I should fancy theory and its application will have its influence on the laborer too.”

cases.sentence: – Да, но постой: – я говорю не о ___, я говорю о науке хозяйства.
cases.explain: «политической экономии» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Yes, but wait a bit. I’m not talking of political economy, I’m talking of the science of agriculture. It ought to be like the natural sciences, and to observe given phenomena and the laborer in his economic, ethnographical. …”
